overall: The AG found no violation: the July 13 emergency meeting qualified as an emergency, and posting notice was not reasonably possible given the short weekend notice. It also recommended (not ordered) that the Board create and approve minutes of that meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board held a July 13 emergency meeting without posting any notice of it.
allegations.key_passage: Although public bodies generally are required to post notice of all meetings, even emergency meetings, in these particular circumstances where the meeting was called on extremely short notice on a weekend, we find that it was not “reasonably possible” for the Board to post notice of its emergency meeting.

allegations.summary: Not raised in the complaint: the three members discussed the matter by telephone rather than in person at a publicly accessible location.
allegations.key_passage: we decline to find a violation for the failure of the three Board members to hold their discussion in person.

allegations.summary: Not raised in the complaint; the AG noted the Board should have created and approved minutes of its July 13 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Finally, although not raised in the  complaint, we note that the Board should have created and approved minutes of its July 13 meeting, and we recommend that the Board do so at this time.
